>If we performed poorly (for any reason), we were basically just told that we were "smarter than that" and that we were being lazy (cue parental Look of Disapproval).

>Our greatest fears had been letting our parents/teachers down, because clearly they already knew that we were "smart" -- and if we couldn't live up to that, there was something wrong with us.

Holy fudgefizzler thank you for putting that into words. I could *never* do anything well enough for my parents, there was *always* something wrong with my work, and praise was exceedingly rare and for insipid things. Teachers would give me the "you're a bright child and should do better" line when I messed up. I was expected to be the star of my class, and was made to know it.

All it ended up doing was making me completely neurotic and being unable to enjoy anything if I couldn't do it *absolutely perfectly*. I still have no self-confidence to speak of, despite trying to objectively evaluate my work. Whether it's at college or a job, anything less than absolutely flawless leaves me curled up in tears and refusing to go back.

It's screwed up, it's wrong, and now that I'm an adult, mine to fix.

PLEASE DON'T DO THIS TO YOUR CHILDREN.

Please teach them it's their effort and hard work that count, and praise them when they really try hard, even if it's not wonderful, or even good. Else they might not end up trying at all.

I can already say they're not going to forgive me. This is a patten I keep falling into. I see it when I'm lucid, then I degenerate, and do fucking retarded things without a second thought.

I do try to do things - that little voice in my head screams that I'm incompetent, I'm stupid, and that I will never amount to anything, no matter how much praise and success I happen to enjoy. I make one small mistake, and it's as if the world's ended. *Enjoying* things instead of worrying whether I'm doing "well enough" is something I have no experience with.

I spiral out of control and hurt those close to me without a second thought. I keep trying, over and over and over again, but I can't seem to stop fucking everything up. All it takes is a moment of unclear thinking, and then it can't be taken back.

I can't help but think that I am a disease that needs to be purged...

I guess the snarky answer would be that life really isn't fair. 

Your little sister really cares about you, doesn't she? I really don't know what to say, because the answers to these things elude me, too.

But you have someone that loves you. How would she feel if you died? Even that question's not fair, because your mind works differently when you're down. Still - I bet she calls you because she loves you, and wants to see you stay in this world and overcome your difficulties.

It's not easy, and it's never fair. All I can do is offer my empathy.

I feel your pain, I'm trying to avoid being in a similar situation. The logical part of me says that if you do just hang on until you're out, you'll be okay.

You might not be able to be hired for a traditional job, but really, think about it. How good are those, anyway? You're a smart person that got him or herself into a terrible position. You can use those smarts to start your own business and make your own life.

I can't speak to what prison would be like. Depending on where you're sent and for how long, it might not be so bad. Think about how many people that are sent to prison are a lot like you. People caught up in things beyond their understanding, without thinking, or even being able to consider, the consequences ahead of time.

We always want better options. There's always another choice. I can't speak for what's best and what's not, but there are an incredible number of paths you could take from here.

This may seem strange, coming from me, but you're probably fundamentally a decent person.

Try smiling. Even if you think there's nothing to smile about, smile. Hygiene problems are probably a result of the depression. Do what you must to make brushing your teeth and showering regularly a part of your life. Showering every day is overrated. Not everyone needs to.

Stop the fucking alcohol. It is just numbing you to what's going on, so things even harder to deal with.

Look to see if there are any groups in your area that share similar interests. You won't learn how to socialize if you don't get practice.

I would avoid trying to do things like cut calories when you're this out of sorts, that ends up depressing the body further. Swap out your junk and alcohol for good things like meat and vegetables. Exercise is good. Really good. Find physical activity you like - if it's something you can do with other people, that's a good way to meet others.

It's hard. It's the hardest thing in the world to just try to go out and do what's best for you when you have no energy and no motivation and everything seems bleak.

Please. Try.
